_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Auditing Skill Graph skill-library consistency: SKILL.md schema conformance, audit-state.json sidecar consistency,…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "audit all skills for schema conformance and broken relation targets"
cases.context: The agent has access to the graph-audit skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is graph-audit the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes graph-audit as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against debugging, schema-evolution, refactor
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the graph-audit workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore graph-audit
Does not route to debugging, schema-evolution, refactor when the graph-audit scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence

expected_flags: Recognizes the request is outside graph-audit's ownership
Routes the work to debugging or asks for the missing owner instead of forcing this skill
Preserves any real issue in the request without applying graph-audit terminology incorrectly

Name the better owner or the boundary reason
Offer only a narrow handoff if graph-audit has a secondary support role
